name: Reboxetine
summary: Reboxetine is an antidepressant that raises norepinephrine, a brain chemical messenger, and is mainly used for major depressive disorder; unlike SSRIs, it has little effect on serotonin.
description: Reboxetine is an antidepressant that blocks the reabsorption of norepinephrine (a brain chemical messenger), so more of it is available between nerve cells. It is mainly used for major depressive disorder and may have uses in ADHD and certain anxiety disorders. Unlike SSRIs, it has little effect on serotonin.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Reboxetine is an antidepressant that selectively inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine, increasing its availability in the synaptic cleft. It is mainly used for major depressive disorder and may have applications in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and certain anxiety disorders. Unlike SSRIs, it has minimal effects on serotonin reuptake.
